einstellungen.text: Twelve fifteen. On your bus, the seats are empty. In the window, they're not.
Three figures. Old coats. Wet hair hanging down over their faces.
Wet footprints shine on the floor. They lead in from the door.
Water drips from the seats behind you. Cold and dark.
You hold your breath. Your breathing is the only sound on the bus. You only look at the window.
Your phone buzzes. Your mom is calling.
“Where are you? It's already past midnight.”
You say just two words: Millbrook Lane.
On the other end, it goes quiet. The line crackles.
“That's where your grandpa grew up. The village is under the reservoir.”
In nineteen ninety-eight, they flooded the valley. Houses, church, school. All underwater.
Then the call drops. No signal.
The window fogs up. From the bottom up, like someone is breathing on it.
In the window, one of the figures leans forward. Toward you.
A cold breath brushes the back of your neck. Like an open fridge.
Then a finger writes on the foggy glass, from the inside. Four letters. Stop.
